intro: Our ramblings on doughnuts and other things.

posts.title: Where to get Apple Cider Donuts near Raleigh this Fall

image.alt: An apple cider donut (a rarity in North Carolina) from The Blue Ox Bakery

body: It’s Fall y’all, and here in North Carolina we usually celebrate with a heat wave. Not this year though, the temperature has finally gone down enough to lull us into a Fallse (see what I did there?) sense of autumnal security.

One of the biggest questions I get around this season revolves around Apple Cider Donuts. Apple Cider Donuts aren’t common in Raleigh. They’re a staple of New England’s Autumn, but we’re too far south to really experience the majesty.
Having said that, we shouldn’t stop trying.

body.heading: Here are 7 places you can get an Apple Cider Donut (or something close) near Raleigh

body.subheading: The Blue Ox Bakery in Raleigh

body: The Apple Cider donuts made by The Blue Ox Bakery might be as close as you can get in the Triangle. They’re made by a *real* New Englander! You can find them in the pastry case over at Little Blue Bakehouse or at one of their Fall Hot Donut Pop Ups. Grabbing a hot apple cider donut at one of the hot donut pop ups is likely the closest we can get to a genuine apple cider donut experience.
Apple Cider is the most popular donut flavor at Kim’s Bakeshop and can be found there every day that they’re open.
Apple Cider Donuts are back on the Monuts menu. You can grab a donut along with coffee and a sandwich for a fancy Fall meal.
Early Bird posted on their socials that they are making cider cake donuts. As the name implies, you should get there early. They run out of things quickly.

This orchard offers apple cider mini-donuts and apple slushies. In the North Carolina heat, that's an optimal choice. The mini-donuts have gained popularity and are offered in various seasonal flavors on weekends throughout most of the year.

On September 19th, Hill Ridge Farms started rolling out their apple cider donuts for the Fall Pumpkin Festival. The festival includes various activities and requires guests to pay admission in order to participate.
Fresh apple cider donut in a few different flavors are available at the Country Store. No admission is required to shop in the store or market area.

body.subheading: Botanist and Barrel in Cedar Grove

body: Will have them available on October 3rd at their 8th Annual Apple Fest. Entry is $5 and includes an apple cider donut.

body.subheading: Freshly Baked by Meg at Daughters Coffee and Books in Durham

body: Meg commented on our Instagram that Daughters Coffee and Books in Durham will have their gluten-free apple cider donuts in stock regularly throughout the Fall.
Did we miss a local spot? Email us at hello@doughnut-days.com, message us on the [Doughnut Days Instagram](https://instagram.com/doughnut_days), or use the [Contact Form](/Contact-Us/).

posts.title: Baked donuts are the wet socks of the pastry world (and the only exception is at Big Dom's Bagel Shop)

image.alt: two vanilla b’donuts held up by anti-baked donut advocate, Maria and companion Dan, in the Page Walker Arts Center garden

body: I’ve had a vendetta against baked donuts for years. I have such strong opinions about how baked donuts are a scourge on our society that I’m 99% sure that if I didn’t censor myself a bit in this post, I’d get canceled.

I loathe baked donuts. For the record, I do know that most baked donuts aren’t horrid. They’re FINE. I hate them on principle. Realistically, what I might hate is misleading marketing in the form of a baked donut. We’ve gone too far though, so the opinion is going to have to hold.

body.heading: Everything That’s Wrong with Baked Donuts

body: A baked donut is a cupcake with the center scooped out and replaced with misery. If there’s a book that featured poor, mistreated orphans they’d be forced to eat baked donuts and it would rank lower than their usual grey gruel. I’m pretty sure I’ve seen a seagull spit out a baked donut in favor of garbage and I completely understand why.

Baked donuts are deceptive. I’ve been bamboozled by so many shops that post perfectly angled photos that make their baked donuts look like fried cake donuts and it pisses me off every time. By definition, donuts are fried. So either fry them up like an adult or tell me they’re donuts baked in sadness, cowards!

If you’re a sadistic prick, I do have a baked donut tag on our [Raleigh Donut Map](/Raleigh-Donut-Map/). You can be wrong and even like them. I’m not here to stop you, but I am going to tell you that if you must get a baked donut, at least do yourself the favor of going somewhere worthwhile.

body.heading: B’Donuts at Big Dom’s Bagel Shop

body: The only place (so far) from which I have ever enjoyed a baked donut is Big Dom’s Bagel Shop in downtown Cary, NC. Big Dom’s set up shop in a former Little Caesars Pizza. One thing that makes this spot unique is that it bakes its bagels in the conveyor belt pizza oven that Little Caesars left behind. They also allow you to order online the day before and grab your order at the Drive Thru window, which is my preferred method. This weekend was our first time going inside the shop itself. The inside is decorated beautifully with standing room by the order counter, there is a small seating area outside with benches (no tables) where you can hang out too.

Big Dom’s has fantastic bagels and bagel sandwiches, but what I appreciate most is that they don’t pretend to have donuts. They have b’donuts (baked donuts). They’re rich and buttery and covered in powdered sugar that gets everywhere. They have an indentation in the center, but not a donut hole, because baked donuts don’t need them. You get all joy and no sadness because this pastry is a masterpiece.

We ordered 2 vanilla b’donuts and a cold brew, for a whopping total of $14 and booked it over to the Page Walker Arts Center garden. If you’re looking for somewhere peaceful to promenade (like a proper Bridgerton) and enjoy your Big Dom’s b’donuts, Page Walker is it. They have a beautiful garden that they put a lot of care into. The building itself is lovely and, if you explore a bit and go towards Cary Town Hall, you’ll even find some benches and tables too.

Big Dom’s Bagel Shop has a sister shop named Faulisi Caffè & Enoteca. They make creations just as lovely as b’donuts, maybe even a little classier. They open just as Big Dom’s is closing and have pizzas, sandwiches, and a little wine shop. The service is exceptional, the space is lovely, and the food is divine. I’m honestly shocked that I don’t see it featured on influencer channels more often. If you are going to be influenced to go anywhere from our accounts, these two spots are solid picks.

posts.title: I can't believe it's Butter Bakery

image.alt: The Butter Bakery stand in Clayton, a yellow fridge painted like a beautiful stick of butter, with a Sold Out notice taped to the door

body: I don’t like getting up early, but my body knows when it’s time for pastries. At 5:50am I woke up ready for Butter Bakery.

Last weekend we went to Clayton to grab coffee and spotted a little butter fridge with a sold out sign on it. Butter Bakery is a self-serve bake stand near Clayton Town Square. It’s restocked a few times a week and draws plenty of interest.

I was baffled, nearing on offended, that we hadn’t seen it before and even more distressed that no one told me about it. It’s like when you “discover” a new band and it turns out all your friends already knew about them and now they all think you’re a giant, out-of-touch nerd.

We ran into the owner, Sara Grace, and her dad (who was sporting a lovely Butter Bakery shirt that us commoners will hopefully be able to purchase soon). The bakery has only been running for a few weeks, but this studio artist and baker has really churned out a winning model.
Here are some good things to know before you go:

list: Stock is limited and they sell out quickly. They were out of chocolate chip cookies within 15 minutes and fully sold out after 1 hour.
They’ve added lattes to the rotation in case you forget the cold brew you made on your kitchen counter.

body: There’s a park and sculpture walk nearby where you can take a casual stroll and put off starting the workday, making the morning the butter half of your day.

posts.title: Avoiding the line at Britt's Donut Shop

image.alt: Britt's Donut Shop at Carolina Beach, surprisingly empty on a rainy day

body: We have been trying to get to Britt’s Donut Shop for years. 5 years to be exact. In April when they were getting ready to open for the season, I excitedly told my hairdresser that this was the year we were finally going to go. She told me they had permanently closed down and then proceeded to cut my bangs too short.

I really appreciate how many people write in to share their donut news, but there’s a reason we fact check things. One of the owners of Britt’s did pass away in October of last year, but the shop still opened this season. My heart can take having too-short bangs, but missing out on Britt’s would have literally killed me.

I have heard how long the lines are at Britt’s and how long people spend waiting. As someone in their thirties or forties, it’s only a matter of time before some younger, hotter donut enthusiast replaces me. I simply can’t afford to wait. So the only remaining option was to go at open.

The drive from Raleigh to Wilmington is about 2 hours. We woke up at 5am to try to leave at 5:30, but left at 6am because even though I don’t have time to wait in a line, I do have time to complain about getting up at 5 in the morning to try to avoid waiting in line. Rainstorms moved through the state, which means our usual summer hellfires were temporarily replaced by slightly milder and damper summer hellfires.

Right around 8am on a rainy Saturday morning, there’s hardly anyone at the Carolina Beach Boardwalk. At the shop there were less than a handful of people in line and plenty of open seating. Britt’s only makes one type of donut: glazed. I love when I don’t have to think about my order. We got a half dozen and a small coffee, which came out at record speed. If they had a gumball machine, it probably would have taken longer for the gumball to drop. They do not have a gumball machine.

Sitting at the counter, you can see the donuts getting fried in what looks like a vessel from the 1930s: industrial, sturdy, and possibly haunted. It’s an impressive and seemingly long-lasting piece of tech that makes the outside of the donuts just a little bit crispy and keeps the inside nice and soft. I think so many people like this place because it feels so unchanged. They’re cash-only, so in a day and age where you can use your phone or retina scan to pay, it’s a nice change of pace. I assume the feeling is different when there’s a line out the door, the floor is wet with seawater, and someone’s sunburned uncle is yelling their order to the teenagers at the counter, but the whole thing felt like a slower, gentler experience. You pay with cash, sit at the counter, get your order and enjoy at your leisure.

Ultimately, this is a lovely donut experience if you’re able to avoid a line or can afford to hire someone to stand in line for you. And while I have no scientific backing for this, I think not having to wait makes a donut taste sweeter.
Happy donut hunting.

posts.title: The 2026 Raleigh Donut Maps are Live
body: Somewhere in 2021 or 2022 I created the Raleigh and Washington DC Donut maps. I posted what I had created on Reddit and one of the first comments I got was that I shouldn’t have wasted my time and made a fried chicken map instead.
What a time to be alive.

Here we are 5 or 6 or some amount of years later, in 2026, with a new, glorious set of [Raleigh Donut Maps](/Raleigh-Donut-Map/). The lack of fried chicken maps still make my heart weep, but we soldier on.

I started this project before AI was common. The amount of digging I did to find and share all of the local donut vendors we have in and around Raleigh is straight up bananas to me now. Hours and hours of work, interacting with folks online, and going out to test out new donut places. Fully worth it, we made a ton of friends, but keeping up with these ventures can be difficult. We dropped off for a bit, I don’t think I’ve updated instagram in at least a year, but we’re back.

For full transparency, this new website was built using Claude. The donut maps were not and our donut data isn’t either. A software engineer and a web accessibility analyst got together, had a baby, and apparently it ended up looking like the page you’re currently navigating. We worked from sketches in notebooks, tweaked everything to make it easier to navigate with a screen reader and keyboard, and generally tried to keep things clean and easy.

The [Raleigh Donut Maps](/Raleigh-Donut-Map/) are built out on Google Maps and also presented as a handy website list. The maps and list both have filters you can use and a handy search tool. We did our best to update the maps with any new locations. If there’s a spot we missed, you can mosey over to our contact form or email us at hello@doughnut-days.com.
It’s nice to be back online. I hope these maps make your life a little sweeter.
